articles.body:
The Rebels moved up from No. 8 to No. 4 in the post-Week 3 AP Top 25 after their 32-24 win over LSU on Saturday night. After Lane Kiffin's Tigers scored 17 straight to tie the game, a fourth-quarter run by Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss turned out to be the winning score.

Ole Miss leapfrogged Indiana, Miami and Ohio State after all three of those teams won over the weekend. LSU dropped from No. 7 to No. 10.

The top three stayed the same as Texas, Georgia and Notre Dame were also all victorious. Between Ohio State and LSU are No. 8 Alabama and No. 9 BYU.

Texas A&M fell from No. 9 to No. 23 after its home loss to Kentucky on Saturday. The Aggies were pushed around by the Wildcats in the 31-21 loss.

SMU fell to No. 22 after its loss to Louisville. The Cardinals jumped up seven spots to No. 16 after the win.

The SEC had two new teams enter the poll in Florida and Mississippi State to set up a loaded Week 4 of ranked matchups in the conference. No. 1 Texas visits No. 14 Tennessee, No. 4 Ole Miss heads to No. 21 Florida, No. 10 LSU hosts No. 21 Texas A&M and No. 19 Missouri goes to No. 24 Mississippi State.

There'd be a fifth game between ranked teams in the league if Oklahoma stayed in the top 25. However, the Sooners dropped out of the poll after their ugly 14-6 win over New Mexico.

articles.title: Nate Sheppard proves point after Stanford's boast on stopping the run
articles.summary: Duke RB Nate Sheppard quieted the talk of Stanford CB Brandon Nicholson with another Heisman-worthy game.
articles.body:
Nate Sheppard has seen the Heisman hype and said he's taking it with "so much grain of salt" this early in the season.

The Duke running back also saw the clip of Stanford cornerback Brandon Nicholson saying no one runs on the Cardinals' defense. The Blue Devils ' offensive line and Sheppard himself proved that wrong on Saturday, and after the 35-7 victory in which he put up 154 rushing yards and three total touchdowns, Sheppard was asked about the clip.

Yeah, so I saw the quote, I think on Wednesday, and then we actually saw the video, I think it was yesterday, on Friday, and it was the type of arrogance he had when he said it, and I think it rubbed the whole offense the wrong way," he said. "We were out there to prove a point."

Prove a point indeed, as the Blue Devils racked up 268 yards on the ground, led by their star running back, who leads the nation in all-purpose and rushing yards after Week 3. He came out strong from the start, eclipsing the 100-yard mark in the second quarter, including a 32-yard touchdown run that showcased his agility and speed and got the team on the board.

It's not exactly Sheppard's personality to look for a challenge. Still, he's already been given plenty this season, including being left off the Doak Walker Award Watch List for best running back in the country. The Louisiana native responded with a meme on Twitter and, to make sure voters were paying attention, was named Doak Walker Award Running Back of the Week after a 227-yard, two-touchdown performance against Tulane.

"I'm not looking for it, but if they're going to give it to me, I'm going to take it and run," Sheppard said.

articles.title: Liverpool can solve one of their main problems with £80m star
articles.summary: Liverpool may have spent more than £600 million over the last couple of seasons but, they still have a few glaring issues among their ranks that need to be s...
articles.body:
Liverpool may have spent more than £600 million over the last couple of seasons but, they still have a few glaring issues among their ranks that need to be solved.

Some problems that they had at the end of the 2025-26 season have obviously been ironed out and fixed but others are going to take a bit more time.

We're also still very early in the season so, once players get fully used to Andoni Iraola's style of play and what he expects from them, things will probably run much smoother.

However, until then, the transfer market could end up being the Reds' best friend or even their worst enemy.

But, thanks to a fresh report that has just emerged, it now seems like £80 million could help them solve one of their main issues.

Crystal Palace would let Adam Wharton exit Selhurst Park for £80 million

Everyone knows that Liverpool's midfield is their weakest area at the moment.

Indeed, they haven't managed to replace Mohamed Salah yet but, with Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola being added to Andoni Iraola's ranks, Liverpool seem to have enough firepower to fill the void he left behind.

Of course, they'd be much better off if they actually managed to bring a natural right-winger in but, after the fees they were being quoted for Ismaila Sarr and Yankuba Minteh, it's not hard to understand why a right-winger wasn't signed.

So, despite Liverpool's attack still needing reinforcement, their midfielders are their main issues.

At the moment, Alexis Mac Allister is their best central midfielder by a country mile with his ability to defend and attack allowing him to become key in Iraola's system.

But, since the Reds still need to shore up their midfield ranks a bit more, the fact that Crystal Palace would be willing to sell Adam Wharton for £80 million will be music to their ears.

"Wharton looks set to be available for a fee in the region of £80m this January, according to some sources," Caught Offside wrote .

"It will be interesting to see what CFC do, but there is an increased urgency to strengthen in the middle of the park, even if there hasn't previously been unanimous backing for Wharton.

"The 22-year-old has also been on the radar of Liverpool."

£80 million is all Liverpool will need to spend to fix their main issue

The Englishman has become one of Palace's most important players over the last few years and, since Elliott Anderson joined Manchester City for £116 million this summer, the £80 million that Pierre Sage wants for Wharton is justified.

His range of passing and ability to stay back and defend are likely two of the key reasons why Liverpool want him.

The fact that he's homegrown is also a massive help as, at the moment, the Reds have managed to fill all of their foreign places in their squad.

Wharton is also only 22 years old so, even though he's already at the top of his game, there's plenty of time for him to grow into an even better player than he already is.

£80 million may seem quite steep but, if it helps solidify Liverpool's ranks and ensures that they can start challenging for silverware again, the Englishman would be worth every penny.

articles.title: Jets, Packers tied 7-7 at halftime
articles.summary: The Jets and Packers have not produced many offensive highlights through 30 minutes of play at a wet MetLife Stadium.
articles.body:
The Jets and Packers have not produced many offensive highlights through 30 minutes of play at a wet MetLife Stadium.

Neither team scored or moved the ball past midfield in the first quarter of the game, but they both found enough footing to post touchdowns in the second quarter. A Packers punt gave the Jets one more chance to put points on the board, but the clock ran out on the half with the Jets near midfield and the score tied 7-7.

The Packers score came on a screen pass to running back MarShawn Lloyd and the Jets answered with a six-yard run by Braelon Allen on the ensuing drive. Packers quarterback Jordan Love is 7-of-12 for 47 yards while Geno Smith is 14-of-23 for 102 yards.

The Packers lost wide receiver Jayden Reed and right tackle Zach Beko-Bewele to injuries on their first possession. Both players have been ruled out for the rest of the game and could be out longer after being carted off the field.

Neither team has turned the ball over thus far and a change on that front could help swing the result in New Jersey.

articles.title: Ja'Marr Chase makes a poster catch to give Bengals 7-3 halftime lead
articles.summary: Ja'Marr Chase has a habit of starting slowly in Week 1 and blowing up in Week 2.
articles.body:
Ja'Marr Chase has a habit of starting slowly in Week 1 and blowing up in Week 2. He had two catches for 12 yards last week in the season opener.

The Bengals receiver made one of the best catches you will ever see with 3:29 left until halftime Sunday. His 32-yard touchdown, despite tight coverage from Derek Stingley , brought back memories of Giants wide receiver Odell Beckham 's catch over Cowboys cornerback Brandon Carr in 2014.

Chase has four catches for 48 yards, and the Bengals lead the Texans 7-3 at halftime in a defensive battle.

The Texans have outgained the Bengals 208 to 156, with three sacks of Joe Burrow . But Houston is 0-for-3 in the red zone, with drives ending at the Cincinnati 16, 18 and 19.

The Texans twice turned it over on downs, including once when holder Kai Kroeger dropped a snap on a chip-shot field goal from the 16-yard line. Kicker Ka'imi Fairbairn kicked a 37-yard field goal with 1:17 remaining in the half.

The Bengals were called for a false start on Dalton Risner on a 58-yard field goal that Evan McPherson made and decided to punt.

Burrow is 12-of-19 for 129 yards and a touchdown, and Tee Higgins has caught four for 72. Chase Brown has seven carries for 42 yards.

Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud has completed 15 of 24 passes for 182 yards. Tight end Dalton Schultz has four catches for 68 yards. David Montgomery has only 10 yards on six carries.

articles.title: Pékerman rompe el silencio sobre James Rodríguez y su llegada a Atlético Nacional: "Es un ganador top"
articles.standfirst: Pékerman se sinceró sobre el regreso de James Rodríguez al FPC y su firma con Nacional
articles.summary: Pékerman se sinceró sobre el regreso de James Rodríguez al FPC y su firma con Nacional
articles.body: El regreso de James Rodríguez al fútbol colombiano para vestir la camiseta de Atlético Nacional sigue generando repercusiones en el ámbito deportivo. En esta ocasión, una de las voces más autorizadas para hablar del volante cucuteño, José Néstor Pékerman, rompió el silencio y compartió sus impresiones sobre este nuevo capítulo en la carrera del mediocampista. Pékerman, quien potenció el talento de James hasta llevarlo a ser el goleador del Mundial de Brasil 2014 y referente indiscutible de la 'Tricolor', valoró la oportunidad de que el futbolista pueda competir en la liga local antes de su retiro. Para el técnico argentino, este paso representa una oportunidad especial en la trayectoria del '10', quien emigró al balompié internacional a una edad muy temprana. “En lo deportivo va a ser muy bueno que él pueda llegar al fútbol nacional, a la liga local, como una despedida, porque el jugador tiene el deseo de poder en algún momento jugar el torneo de su país, y por su actividad, por haberse ido tan joven, no ha tenido la oportunidad”, afirmó el estratega. Pese a las dudas que puedan surgir por el ritmo competitivo o la falta de continuidad que traía en los últimos meses, Pékerman enfatizó que la mentalidad de James marcará una diferencia sustancial en el vestuario verdolaga. Lo definió como un «líder futbolístico clave» y un competidor nato cuya presencia eleva el rendimiento de sus compañeros. “Nunca dejó de pensar que hay que ganar y siempre para él fue una prioridad. Los compañeros saben que están al lado de un top, de un ganador top. Se sienten que van a estar a su nivel, aunque no lo tenga, pero sienten un respaldo enorme”, sostuvo Pékerman, agregando que su exigencia impulsará a todo el plantel a mantener un estándar elevado. Pékerman concluyó señalando que confía en el compromiso profesional de James para ponerse a punto físicamente y responder a las exigencias de la competición actual. Según el entrenador, el futbolista tiene claro que en el fútbol de alto rendimiento no se puede aflojar, por lo que proyecta un paso exitoso de Rodríguez en su etapa con Atlético Nacional.

articles.title: Colombia vence a Nigeria en el último suspiro y clasifica a semifinales del Mundial Sub-20
articles.summary: La Selección Colombia Femenina Sub-20 sigue escribiendo páginas doradas en el fútbol internacional. En un agónico y disputado encuentro en el estadio Miejski LKS de Lodz, el conjunto 'tricolor' derrotó 1-0 a Nigeria en los cuartos de final del Mundial Sub-20 de Polonia, asegurando su tiquete entre las cuatro mejores selecciones del planeta.
articles.body: La Selección Colombia Femenina Sub-20 sigue escribiendo páginas doradas en el fútbol internacional. En un agónico y disputado encuentro en el estadio Miejski LKS de Lodz, el conjunto 'tricolor' derrotó 1-0 a Nigeria en los cuartos de final del Mundial Sub-20 de Polonia, asegurando su tiquete entre las cuatro mejores selecciones del planeta. El trámite del partido no fue sencillo para las dirigidas por Carlos Paniagua. Desde los primeros minutos, Nigeria hizo sentir su potencia física y velocidad, generando serias opciones de peligro en el área colombiana. La guardameta Luisa Agudelo se erigió como la gran figura del primer tiempo al ahogar el grito de gol africano en al menos dos intervenciones decisivas, destacando un atajadón a mano cambiada tras un remate de media distancia de Ramotalahi Kareem. Pese a afrontar el encuentro con bajas sensibles —como la ausencia de Maithé López por lesión y Lina Arboleda por suspensión—, Colombia mantuvo el orden táctico y apeló a la paciencia ante la ferocidad del rival. El choque cambió de ritmo en la recta final de la segunda mitad. Al minuto 76, la jueza central mostró la tarjeta roja directa a la nigeriana Kafayat Mafisere tras una falta antideportiva sobre Samantha Rodríguez, dejando al equipo africano con diez jugadoras en cancha. Cuando el partido parecía encaminado a la prórroga, apareció la astucia y garra colombiana en el tiempo de adición (90+1'). Juana Ortegón filtró una pelota limpia al espacio. Valerín Loboa disputó la posición contra la zaga rival. Tras un primer remate atajado por la portera y un bote afortunado, Loboa punteó el balón para decretar el 1-0 definitivo y desatar la locura cafetera. Con este triunfo, el combinado nacional clasifica a semifinales y buscará superar su mejor registro histórico en un Mundial Sub-20. El duelo por el pase a la gran final se disputará el próximo miércoles a las 11:30 a. m. (hora colombiana), donde las 'cafeteras' enfrentarán al equipo ganador del cruce entre Corea del Norte y Canadá.

articles.title: World Series of Darts Finals: England's Ross Smith beats Gerwyn Price
articles.summary: England's Ross Smith shocks Wales' Gerwyn Price to win World Series of Darts Finals as Luke Littler's clean-sweep dream ends in last eight in Amsterdam.
articles.body:
Englishman Ross Smith won the final six legs to produce a shock 11-5 victory over two-time former winner Gerwyn Price in the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.

It was just a second major title for the 37-year-old, whose only previous success at this level of the PDC World Tour came at the European Championship in 2022.

But the world number 14 overpowered his loftier opponent with a barrage of 180s, hitting 11 maximums, compared to Welshman Price's five, to finish a deserved winner.

It was a fitting finale to a tournament of shocks that saw world champion Luke Littler lose in the quarter-finals and miss out on his quest to claim a clean sweep of the major PDC titles in 2026.

Littler could boycott Dutch events over booing

Littler seals dramatic final-leg win over Aspinall

Thousands at darts audition to take on Luke Littler

"Honestly, I am made up with the win. I am just so happy," said Smith, who suffered first-round exits in New Zealand and Australia in his only two other appearances in the 2026 World Series.

"You are playing Gerwyn Price - one of the best players in the world. You have got to up your game."

Smith beat Northern Ireland's Josh Rock 10-7 in the last eight and Dutch hope Gian van Veen 11-8 in the semi-finals to give himself a shot at the £100,000 winner's prize.

Price, meanwhile, made it past England's James Wade in the quarter-finals before beating compatriot Jonny Clayton - Littler's conqueror - in the last four.

The 2020 and 2022 winner won back-to-back legs to make it 5-5 against Smith in the final but was hanging on as his opponent continued to score heavily albeit with a lower checkout success.

Smith, however, was far more clinical after the interval, winning the next three legs, including back-to-back checkouts of 127 and 123.

The checkouts cooled but Smith won a succession of scrappy legs to seal victory as Price's game deserted him.

Earlier, Littler's bid for a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 was ended by a 10-4 defeat by Clayton in the quarter-finals.

The world number one had followed his World Championship triumph at Alexandra Palace in January by winning titles at the World Masters, UK Open, Premier League, World Cup of Darts and World Matchplay.

But after threatening to boycott events in the Netherlands after being roundly booed by the crowd during his last-16 win over Nathan Aspinall, the Warrington-based player failed to produce his best darts against Clayton.

articles.title: World Series of Darts Finals: Ross Smith thrashes Gerwyn Price in final after Luke Littler's dream of clean sweep ends
articles.summary: Gerwyn Price "does not care" if he never wins another major as he prepares to head to Tenerife following "absolute rubbish" defeat to Ross Smith in World Series of Darts Finals; Luke Littler knocked out in last eight as hopes of clean sweep of titles dashed
articles.body:
Smith won the last six legs, fired in 11 maximums, recorded back-to-back ton-plus finishes and went at 46 per cent on his doubles as he overwhelmed Price in Amsterdam on Sunday night to claim his second PDC major, after the 2022 European Championship.

Price, who missed a host of doubles in the back end of the match as his checkout percentage dropped to 26, has seven PDC majors in total, including three Grand Slams and the 2021 World Championship, but none since the World Series Finals in 2022.

Speaking bluntly afterwards on ITV4, the Welshman said: "I am playing some good darts, I am earning some good money. If I never win a major again I really don't care as long as I am doing well.

"I am gutted I've lost but if I never win another major then I have a good family, I have invested all my money. I really don't mind. I will be gutted for half an hour but on Tuesday I'll be in Tenerife.

"I was absolute rubbish in that final but don't take anything away from Ross. He was brilliant and took his opportunities."

Smith stars in Amsterdam as Littler crashes out

While Smith celebrates his fifth trophy of the season - this triumph in the Netherlands follows the Hungarian Darts Open and International Darts Open on the European Tour and a couple of Players Championship events - Littler is processing a shock defeat.

Having won the first five majors of the year - as well as the World Cup of Darts for England alongside compatriot Luke Humphries - Littler was hoping to claim all 11, only to be trounced 10-4 by Jonny Clayton in the quarter-finals.

Smith overcame Josh Rock in the last eight before dumping out remaining home hope Gian van Veen in the last four, while Price surged towards the end of matches to eliminate James Wade and Clayton before being floored by Smith.

Smith said: "It feels a bit mad, to be fair! I am absolutely made up with the win. I am so happy. [Price] is one of the best in the world, so to beat him you have to up your game.

"I always say in my interviews that I take each game as it comes. I play one game at a time. They are all finals and I give it my all. That is working for me at the moment."

articles.title: Jayden Daniels suffers devastating arm injury, leaves game on cart
articles.summary: The Commanders quarterback appeared to dislocate his left arm against the Cowboys.
articles.body:
Jayden Daniels was having a very good game against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 2. Then, on the final play of the first half, while trying to run one extra play before attempting a field goal, Daniels went down with a devastating arm injury.

Daniels took the snap and had his foot stepped on by his guard. As he stumbled and tried to regain his balance, he put his left arm out to steady himself. The pressure appeared to dislocate his elbow. It looked similar to the injury he suffered last November.

Video is below. Tom Brady , who was calling the game for Fox, couldn't help but exclaim, "Oh sh–" when he saw the replay. It may be uncomfortable to watch.

Daniels tried to run off the field, but went down and was carted off the field.

Daniels suffered a leg injury against the Cowboys last season . He also dealt with a left elbow injury last season . After not missing a game in his first season on his way to Rookie of the Year, he only played in seven games last season. The Commanders lost their season opener to the Philadelphia Eagles .

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers blames himself after Steelers' offense struggles again in loss to Patriots
articles.summary: A year ago, Aaron Rodgers engineered a drive at Gillette Stadium that helped the Pittsburgh Steelers beat the team that went on to represent the AFC in the S...
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. (AP) — A year ago, Aaron Rodgers engineered a drive at Gillette Stadium that helped the Pittsburgh Steelers beat the team that went on to represent the AFC in the Super Bowl.

That version of Rodgers wasn't anywhere to be found in Sunday's 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots . Instead, the future Hall of Famer looked every bit like a 42-year-old playing his last NFL season.

Rodgers wasn't solely to blame. The Steelers' offensive line surrendered four sacks, while veteran wide receiver DK Metcalf had another rough day. But Rodgers pointed to his own shortcomings.

"As players, we've got to take ownership. My performance wasn't good enough and a lot of guys on offense weren't good enough," Rodgers said after finishing 23 of 39 for 187 yards. "We've got to start by looking at ourselves, not point the finger."

Through two games, Rodgers has thrown one touchdown pass in 79 attempts. The offensive issues that plagued coach Mike McCarthy's Steelers during their Week 1 win over Atlanta showed up again.

During the second quarter, New England 's Christian Elliss delivered a blind-side sack of Rodgers, leading to a 36-yard loss. Rodgers shrugged off the hard hit.

"I've learned you've got to get up quickly, number one, so they don't send anybody out to get you," Rodgers said. "That was definitely a shot. I haven't taken too many of those in our career because usually I have a feeling if we're picked up or not picked up. That was a lapse in communication obviously there."

Pittsburgh still had its chances in New England's home opener. Drake Maye was intercepted on the first series of the second half, and the Patriots' Andy Borregales missed a field-goal attempt from 47 yards.

The Steelers failed to turn either of those opportunities into points. Following the New England turnover, Rodgers misfired on third-and-6, leading to a punt. After the missed kick, Metcalf dropped a pass on third down.

Metcalf caught only four of his nine targets for 27 yards.

"It's frustrating, for sure," Rodgers said. "Our defense has been playing great. They've been holding teams to 13 points per game through two games, and offensively, we're averaging eight points per game. That's not winning football."

With Pittsburgh trailing 13-3 in the fourth quarter, Christian Barmore sacked Rodgers, leading to a fumble and a 19-yard scoop-and-score by Elijah Ponder.

Later in the quarter, the Steelers turned it over again when rookie Germie Bedard failed to secure a pass from Rodgers and Patriots rookie Gabe Jacas came away with the interception.

"He created some separation, made some contested catches, and then made a rookie play," Rodgers said of Bedard. "He's a good kid, and cares about it. We're going to need him to keep improving."

articles.title: Jayden Daniels injury: Commanders QB carted off after elbow injury
articles.summary: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels appeared to suffer a significant elbow injury against the Cowboys
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels appeared to suffer another injury to his left elbow just before halftime of Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys .

With the Commanders facing 3rd-and-goal inside the Dallas 5-yard line, and without a timeout remaining, Dan Quinn kept his offense on the field to try in a 17-10 game led by the Cowboys. Daniels began the play under center, and seemed to trip over the linemen in front of him, using his left arm to try and brace himself when he fell.

After the play, Daniels struggled to get to his feet before going back down to the turf at AT&T Stadium. Eventually, the cart came out for Daniels and he was taken off the field, with an aircast on his left arm:

The injury was rather gruesome to watch on replays, during which Tom Brady on FOX Sports let an expletive slip while seeing the replay himself. We are not embedding that replay here, but you can watch the replay to see the injury if you wish.

Daniels missed most of the second half of the 2025 season after dislocating that same left elbow. He made his way back for Week 14 after initially injuring it in Week 9, but Daniels hurt the elbow again and was shut down for the rest of the season.

articles.title: Studs and duds from Houston’s 20-6 loss to the Bengals
articles.summary: Here are our studs and duds following the Houston Texans' 20-6 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals to drop to 0-2 for the second straight year.
articles.body:
For the second straight season, the Houston Texans have started the year with an 0-2 record after falling to the Cincinnati Bengals .

This loss looked completely different than their season opener as the defense had a pretty good day, but the offense could not get going.

The main problem with Houston's offense was the lack of a run game. Cincinnati completely stuffed running back David Montgomery , who finished the day with only 10 yards, his second-lowest ever in a game he has started.

Montgomery was also not involved in the passing game with only two catches for 14 yards.

However, Houston's defense showed up in this game with a total of five sacks spread across six players. The Texans also had a total of 10 quarterback hits. Nonetheless, they still had problems in the secondary containing the Bengals' wide receiver duo, Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase. Chase put up 75 yards and two touchdowns while Higgins was the leading receiver with 95 yards on 10 targets.

Here are the studs and duds from Houston's second loss of the season, including quarterback C.J. Stroud , who had a promising day and running back David Montgomery, who did not do much in this game.

C.J. Stroud caught a lot of strays after the Texans' loss to the Buffalo Bills , after losing two fumbles. This did not look like a good matchup for him going against a defense who just had four forced fumbles in their season opener. However, Stroud responded by never turning the ball over, exercising smart decision-making and finished the game with 353 passing yards, which is his second-most in a loss in his career.

Even though the offense was the problem in this game, Stroud is not to blame.

After the debut he had with the Texans, Montgomery only put up 24 scrimmage yards. No, not rushing. Total.

He only had six rushing attempts and did not do much with those opportunities. Woody Marks actually had more attempts than him, although Marks actually ended up with less yards.

The run game just was not working for Houston in this game, but that is what doomed their offense.

A star running back should not have a performance like this. Then again, his offensive coordinator should get him more involved instead of having him sit on the bench for multiple drives when nothing seems to be working.

Someone had to step up with top receiver Nico Collins out in this game. Schultz did everything the Texans needed him to do. On 14 targets, he had 12 receptions for 140 yards, both of which are career highs. Even though he was not able to get into the end zone, this was an impressive performance from Schultz, especially when everyone knew he would be Stroud's top target going into this game.

With Collins down, Hutchinson especially became the top wide receiver on the roster and he was the most targeted wide receiver in this game. However, despite being targeted nine times, he only had three receptions for 37 yards.

His 33.3 percent catch percentage is his lowest catch percentage in a game with at least three receptions in his entire career. Houston really needed more of him in this game.

Will Anderson was all over the field in this game with eight total tackles, including four solo tackles, three tackles for loss and two sacks. He also had two quarterback hits and defended a pass. Especially after the game Houston's defense had as a unit against the Buffalo Bills , the Texans really needed their top defender to show out.

A punter has two jobs: punt the football and be the holder on field goals and extra points. What was he doing on Houston's field goal attempt to start the second quarter?

Not only did it cost the Texans an easy three points, but it also allowed Cincinnati to gain some momentum and they were eventually able to get a touchdown on the board. This was a very, very bad play by Kroeger. He also only averaged 41.4 yards per punt, which is not great either.

Al-Shaair led the Texans in tackles with 12 total tackles, including six solo tackles. He now has 20 tackles on the season, which puts him well on pace to pass his career-high of 163 tackles from 2023 with the Tennessee Titans .

Like Hutchinson, Wayne got a lot of balls thrown his way but did not do much with them.

Stroud targeted Wayne seven times, but he finished the game with just two receptions for 33 yards. This actually was the best game of his career as far as receiving yards goes, but the Texans still needed more from their third-year receiver in this one.

articles.title: Cubs' Alex Bregman hospitalized after getting hit in face with foul ball
articles.summary: Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman was taken to the hospital after being struck in the face by a foul ball during Sunday's game.
articles.body:
Alex Bregman walked off the field Sunday, Sept. 20 with a towel pressed to his face and blood running down his cheek. The Chicago Cubs third baseman was hit in the face by a foul ball as he waited in the on-deck circle in the top of the fourth inning against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball park.

Bregman was taken to a local hospital for further testing after the scare in Cincinnati. After the 9-1 win , Cubs manager Craig Counsell told reporters the ball hit Bregman in the cheekbone, which is swollen, and left a cut on his face. Bregman was evaluated for broken bones.

It happed with two outs and the Cubs leading 5-0. Michael Busch checked his swing on a 1-2 pitch from Reds right-hander Luis Mey , and the ball ricocheted toward Bregman. He dropped to the ground immediately , clutching his face, then got up and walked to the clubhouse under his own power. There was no official diagnosis.

Before the injury, Bregman had done damage to the Reds. He drove in a run with a first-inning single, then walked and scored in the Cubs' four-run third inning.

The 32-year-old is hitting .260 with 26 home runs, 88 RBIs and an .801 OPS this season. He signed a five-year, $175 million contract with Chicago last winter. The three-time All-Star won two World Series with the Astros .

The timing is the problem for Bregman and the Cubs. Chicago is on the verge of clinching a playoff berth, needing just one win or an Arizona Diamondbacks loss to lock in wild card spot. If Bregman needs time away, the Cubs have Matt Shaw and Pedro Ramirez to fill in at third base. Neither has Bregman's experience in a playoff race.

Any fracture would change the outlook considerably. Facial fractures around the cheek bone or eye socket can sideline a player for weeks, and a hitter usually has to be cleared before he can face live pitching again.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels injury update: What happened to the Commanders QB?
articles.summary: Disaster struck at the worst possible moment for the former rookie of the year.
articles.body:
Jayden Daniels was a ray of sunshine for a franchise accustomed to season-destroying storms. The second overall pick of the 2024 NFL Draft made an immediate impact for the Washington Commanders . He was offensive rookie of the year as he led his team to a shocking spot in the NFC Championship Game.

Then, because the Commanders cannot have nice things, the problems piled up. Injury marred his 2025. Coupled with one of the league's worst defenses, Washington plummeted out of the playoffs with a 5-12 record.

Daniels was efficient in his team's 24-22 opening day loss to the Philadelphia Eagles . He was primed to lead the Commanders in a shootout against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 2. Then, disaster struck.

On third-and-goal on the final play of the first half, Daniels took the snap under center. Before he could drop back, center Nick Allegretti stepped on his foot, forcing him to stumble backward. While he was still able to get a desperation throw off -- it fell incomplete -- he braced himself awkwardly with his left, non-throwing hand, causing his elbow to bend awkwardly and bringing trainers out onto the field.

Daniels was carted off the field while players had already made their exit to the locker room for the mid-game break. He has been ruled out for the rest of Week 2.

Who is the Commanders backup QB if Daniels can't play?

Washington has one of the best backups in the league after re-signing Marcus Mariota to a one year, $7 million contract in the offseason. The former Heisman Trophy winner is capable of bringing high value replacement level play while keeping the dual threat pages of offensive coordinator David Blough 's playbook open. Mariota was just 2-6 as a starter for the Commanders last season. However, his 0.072 expected points added (EPA) per dropback were 24th best among 37 qualified quarterbacks , just ahead of Daniels that season.

articles.title: Travis Kelce was victimized by a Ponzi scheme. Here's what to know about it
articles.summary: Travis Kelce was among the victims of a multi-million dollar Ponzi scheme. Here's more to know about it.
articles.body:
Travis Kelce was the Kansas City Chiefs ' leading receiver during their impressive Week 1 win over the Denver Broncos , but he found himself making headlines for other reasons following the game.

Kelce was listed by prosecutors as a victim of a multi-million-dollar Ponzi scheme that was prosecuted in St. Louis, according to a St Louis-based KMOV investigative reporter who was in the courtroom when his name was read .

Kelce has not yet addressed the case, and it isn't clear when or if he will.

Here's what to know about the situation.

Cheerleaders, celebrities, fans and mascots at NFL games during 2026 season

Full details of Ponzi scheme that victimized Travis Kelce, others

Little was said about Kelce in court, other than him being named among at least 64 victims in the fraud case, according to the report.

Kelce's name is not included in the indictment or judgement in the case, both of which were obtained by USA TODAY Sports. Victim impact statements in the case were sealed, and the details of how much Kelce lost as part of the scheme were not disclosed.

Kelce was listed as an investor in a fund created by Swiftarc, which was founded by the defendant in the case, Siddarth Jawahar, according to a 2021 Forbes article . Basketball players Tim Hardaway Jr., Gary Harris and Mason Plumlee were also listed as investors in the fund by Forbes, but it wasn't immediately clear if they were also victims of the fraud scheme.

Jawahar "took tens of millions of dollars from his investors" instead of making promised investments on their behalf, as the indictment obtained by USA TODAY Sports outlined.

Jawahar then used money acquired from new investors to pay off his previous investors. He then used the remainder to fund "extravagant lifestyle expenses, including payments for flights on private planes, stays at luxury hotels, and expensive outings at lavish restaurants."

Jawahar, 38, pleaded guilty to three counts of wire fraud, according to court documents obtained by USA TODAY Sports. He was sentenced by U.S. District Judge Zachary M. Bluestone to 11 years in prison and will also be required to pay $31.35 million in restitution to his victims.

articles.title: Titans players react to Eagles fans packing Nissan Stadium
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans' fans were clearly outnumbered by visiting fans in Nissan Stadium during a 24-20 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans fans did not win the home attendance battle in Week 2.

They were widely outnumbered by visiting fans in a 24-20 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles at Nissan Stadium on Sept. 20.

Just before kickoff, the stadium was mostly covered in Eagles green. More Titans blue filled in by the first quarter, but Philly fans still seemed to make up 60% to 70% of the 68,567 paid attendance.

They exploded when Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts slammed the door on the Titans late, hitting Darius Cooper for a 3-yard go-ahead touchdown pass with nine seconds remaining in the fourth quarter.

Inside Titans vs Eagles best photos in hottest game at Nissan Stadium

"I'm going to be real. I've been here. We've been 3-14 here the last two years. There have been a lot of games where it's kind of been like that," said Titans linebacker Cedric Gray , who finished with four tackles and a TFL in 30 snaps after returning from concussion protocol. "I'm kind of used to it. It really doesn't bother me. We've got to start winning some games so we can turn that around."

It hasn't been unusual for visiting fans to take over Nissan Stadium the past few seasons. The Titans haven't drawn huge crowds, considering their struggles. And because Nashville's a popular vacation spot, visitors use the chance to see the city and catch a game.

The Titans (0-2) led 20-17 with 1:56 remaining after a Joey Slye 33-yard field goal. At that point, their fans were alive with the Eagles (2-0) on the ropes.

At other times, it felt a little more like a road game for the home team.

Titans guard Peter Skoronski said the offense used its sound cadence "once or twice."

"We have to give (Titans fans) something to show up for, something they're proud of and will pack the stadium for," Skoronski said. "You hate to see the away team take over. Credit to the (home) fans that were there. I thought they did a good job. We felt them at times when we made plays, third downs here and there."

articles.title: Dismal first half dooms Indiana Fever in pivotal loss to Washington Mystics
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever had a poor first half, perhaps worst of the season, and couldn't quite overcome a dismal performance. Here's what we learned.
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS — The Indiana Fever played their biggest game of the season to date Sunday, a late-season clash with the Washington Mystics that carried heavy implications for their postseason future and a potential shot at securing a top-four seed and homecourt advantage.

And when presented with this opportunity … the Fever face-planted, dropping a dreadful 93-77 decision at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. Caitlin Clark had 25 points on 20 shots. Kelsey Mitchell added 22 points on 20 shots.

Indiana is now 27-15, a full game behind Atlanta for fourth and just one game ahead of Dallas , New York and Washington. It closes out the season with a home-and-home vs. Minnesota , which needs to win at least one of those final two games to secure the No. 1 seed.

Here's what I liked and disliked, and what the loss means.

Indiana Fever face Washington Mystics at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis

What I liked in the Indiana Fever 's loss to Washington Mystics

Raven Johnson got extended first-half minutes and replaced Lexie Hull in the starting lineup out of halftime. The rookie guard is a spark plug on the floor, particularly on the defensive end. She finished with six points and a plus-1 rating.

The halftime entertainment involved dogs catching frisbees.

What I disliked in the Indiana Fever 's loss to Washington Mystics

The lack of energy and enthusiasm out of the gates was stunning. This felt like a playoff game coming in, but the Fever looked the part of a team whose ticket had already been punched, leaving them with nothing to play for. Sure, there were some glimmers of life in the second half, but it was too little, too late with how deplorable they were defensively.

Basically everything about the first half. The Fever were horrendous from the jump, missing their first five shots from the field while allowing the Mystics to four straight 3s as they raced out to an eight-point lead less than five minutes in and 15 at the end of the first.

First-half scoring beyond Clark and Mitchell. Make no mistake, the Fever's two MVP hopefuls were not great, shooting a combined 7 for 23 (3 for 12 from 3) … but they still combined for 24 of the team's first 30 points. Everyone else was a combined 2 for 14. And it wasn't just that Indiana wasn't hitting shots. It looked lost on offense, with players taking turns either going 1-on-1 or over-passing as the shot clock ticked down. No one beyond Mitchell and Clark seemed willing to take charge. Bizarre to see.

Fever defense: Still not great. The Mystics shot 64.7% in the first half and 56.9% for the game. Yikes. Indiana's offense found some traction in the third quarter, scoring 31 points … but the defense allowed 26.

Aliyah Boston foul trouble. I'll preface this by saying I thought the fourth foul early in the third was kinda bogus (maybe she caught the shooter on the head as her arm came down?). But she picked up two first-quarter fouls, then picked up her third 18 seconds after checking back in for the second quarter. The Fever desperately needed Boston on the floor, because forward Kiki Iriafen ate them alive inside.

The lack of frontcourt depth. Been a problem all season and was especially noticeable Sunday. Mercedes Russell went 0-for-4 from the field, committed three fouls and was a minus-8 (she had a few rough possessions defensively). Monique Billings played 3:52, posted a minus-6 and, most notably was beaten by Kiki Iriafen for back-to-back offensive rebounds on the same play. Myisha Hines-Allen , who provided a necessary spark in Toronto Friday, managed two field goal attempts, turned it over twice and pulled in four rebounds.

The Fever wings. Sophie Cunningham 's most notable contribution in the first half was getting beat on a drive to the basket and fouling the shooter as she passed by. Lexie Hull played 5:55 in the first quarter, missing a field goal and pulling in two rebounds. Hull did not check back in until the 1:52 mark of the third; Cunningham did not return until the 6:32 mark of the fourth quarter − and she promptly doinked a 3-pointer off the backboard and lost track of a court-length pass from Clark, resulting in a turnover.

What the Indiana Fever's loss to Washington Mystics means

Indiana is now 27-15 and no longer controls its own destiny for homecourt advantage.

The Fever are a full game behind Atlanta for fourth and just one game ahead of Dallas, New York and Washington. It closes out the season with a home-and-home vs. Minnesota, which needs to win at least one of those final two games to secure the No. 1 seed.

articles.title: What Bears QB Caleb Williams said after his injury vs. Vikings
articles.summary: Bears CB Malik Muhammad shared Caleb Williams' message to him after the QB suffered a hamstring injury vs. the Vikings.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears suffered a brutal loss to the Minnesota Vikings , which also unfortunately included quarterback Caleb Williams , who exited in the fourth quarter with a hamstring injury.

It was a scary situation in real time, where Williams went down on an attempted run in the red zone -- for what looked like a sure-fire touchdown -- and grabbed his hamstring and screamed in agony. Williams had to be helped off the field by trainers and was carted to the locker room, where he gave the thumbs up to the Soldier Field crowd cheering him on.

After the game, Bears rookie cornerback Malik Muhammad talked about the mood on the sideline after Williams went down with an injury, and it sums up how every Bears fan felt in the moment.

Photos from Bears' historic 59-37 win over Panthers in Week 1

"I was worried," Muhammad said. "If No. 18 gets hurt, I'm worried. The whole stadium was worried -- maybe the whole world."

Williams will have imaging done on his right hamstring on Monday, which will determine the severity and how much time he'll likely miss. But head coach Ben Johnson said his quarterback was in "good spirits" after the game, where he was spotted by reporters walking around the locker room with perhaps a slight limp.

Muhammad spoke with Williams after the game, and he shared the encouraging message from Williams about his health.

"He should be good. I asked him after the game if he's going to be good. He's going to be good," Muhammad said, adding that Williams is "always in good spirits."

When Williams exited with his hamstring injury, he was replaced by backup Tyson Bagent , who nearly led a game-winning drive in the final minute that fell just short in a 9-3 loss to the Vikings.

articles.title: Caleb Williams injury update gives Bears reason for optimism
articles.summary: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams went down with a hamstring injury in Week 2.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears were fed a healthy dose of humble pie in Week 2, losing to the Minnesota Vikings , 9-3, after a 59-point performance in the season opener a week ago. But even worse for the Bears was an injury to star quarterback Caleb Williams .

Williams went down with a hamstring injury on Sunday afternoon, and was unable to return. He is set to undergo further testing on Monday to determine the full extent of his injury.

While we wait for an official update from the team, there were some positive signs in the locker room following the game.

According to eye witnesses, Williams was up and "walking around " walking around in good spirits ."

Caleb Williams Showing Positive Signs After Hamstring Injury

Ian Rapoport of ESPN and the NFL Network shared the latest on Williams after Sunday's massive injury scare, writing along with Bears insider Adam Jahns.

Jahns revealed, "Williams came through the locker room while the media was present. He was walking under his own power, no crutches or anything , maybe a slight limp."

No crutches and walking under his own power is a positive sign for Williams, but we will not know more until the team evaluates him further on Monday afternoon. If he avoids any long-term injury, it's a major win for the Bears who were making massive strides in the right direction during the offseason and training camp.

articles.title: Game Discussion: Milwaukee Brewers (97-58) @ Baltimore Orioles (75-80)
articles.summary: Jacob Misiorowski, Brewers look for series sweep on Sunday Night Baseball
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers are going for a series sweep in Baltimore tonight, as ace Jacob Misiorowski will toe the rubber for Sunday Night Baseball, Milwaukee's first Sunday night game since the MLB Little League Classic in Williamsport, Pennsylvania, one month ago.

The Brewers, at 97-58 on the season, have also officially tied their franchise record for wins in a season at 97. With one week to go in the regular season, they'll have seven chances to set a new record, and they're also just three wins away from the first 100-win season in franchise history.

The aforementioned Misiorowski is looking for his 16th win of the season tonight in what is likely his penultimate start of 2026. The NL Cy Young frontrunner, Miz is 15-5 with a 1.89 ERA, 2.19 FIP, and 243 strikeouts across 166 1/3 innings, totaling 5.9 bWAR. In his last outing against the Pirates, he went five scoreless innings, allowing five hits and a walk while striking out seven. This marks his first career appearance against Baltimore.

He's made 26 starts this season, with a 9-4 record, 3.65 ERA, 4.57 FIP, and 118 strikeouts over 145 2/3 innings. articles.title: Jayden Daniels elbow injury history: Inside Commanders QB's arm ailments that have derailed young NFL career
articles.summary: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels suffered yet another injury to his non-throwing elbow against the Cowboys.
articles.body:
Commanders QB Jayden Daniels had a lost second season in the NFL, dealing with knee, hamstring and elbow injuries that kept him off the field more than he was on it.

Hoping for a bounce-back season, Daniels saw the same nightmare unfold again on Sunday.

The third-year quarterback suffered a gruesome injury to the same non-throwing elbow at the end of the first half against the Cowboys , requiring a cart to get back to the locker room.

Here's a closer look at Daniels' elbow injury history.

Nov. 2, 2025: Daniels dislocates elbow vs. Seahawks

Daniels first suffered a gruesome injury to his non-throwing elbow during a "Sunday Night Football" game against the Seahawks in 2025. The Commanders quarterback, who had already missed time with hamstring and knee injuries earlier in the season, appeared to be in serious pain as he gave way to backup Marcus Mariota once again.

Despite the gruesomeness of the injury, the news after the game was mostly positive. Because Daniels' injury was to his non-throwing elbow and there was limited damage, a quick return was possible. The second-year quarterback only missed three games (four weeks) before getting back on the field against the Vikings .

Dec. 7, 2025: Daniels shut down after aggravating elbow

The quick return didn't work out for Daniels, as he landed hard on his left elbow during an interception return by the Vikings and was shut down for the remainder of the season after the game.

While Daniels avoided re-dislocating the elbow, the Commanders made the decision to end his season knowing he had battled through knee, hamstring and elbow injuries.

Sept. 20, 2026: Daniels carted off with elbow injury

In an unfortunate twist of fate, Daniels suffered another gruesome injury to the same elbow at the end of the first half of Sunday's game against the Cowboys.

The Commanders quarterback stumbled back after being stepped on and tried to brace his fall by stretching out his left arm, but the impact forced a potential dislocation or hyperextension of his elbow. The injury left Daniels in serious pain, and he left the field on a cart.

The good news once again is that Daniels is dealing with an injury to his non-throwing elbow, which should allow for a much speedier recovery than an injury to his throwing elbow, the re-injury after four weeks last season could serve as a reminder for the Commanders to be cautious about bringing him back in the near future.

articles.title: J.K. Dobbins injury: Latest news on Broncos running back after exiting Jaguars game
articles.summary: Denver Broncos running back J.K. Dobbins suffered an injury in the third quarter of Week 2’s matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos looked to open their 2026 home schedule with a Week 2 win over the 1-0 Jacksonville Jaguars . They lost to them last year at home by a score of 34-20 in Week 15.

Unfortunately, running back J.K. Dobbins suffered an apparent left leg injury during Sunday's game versus Jacksonville. The injury occurred near the end of the third quarter with the Broncos trailing 13-6.

Dobbins had 10 carries for 36 yards before the injury. Sam Jane of the Denver Post reported the injury on X, saying that Dobbins is questionable to return with a hamstring injury.

As the game goes on, it will be Tyler Badie getting most of the reps at RB1. RJ Harvey is inactive for the game with a hamstring injury, so Denver is really hurting at the position on Sunday.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels leaves with elbow injury
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels left the Week 2 game on the final play of the second quarter due to a left elbow injury.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels (elbow, arm) left the Week 2 game on the final play of the second quarter due to a left elbow injury.

Daniels attempted to brace himself from going down, using his left arm, and it gave way, similar to last season against the Seattle Seahawks when he suffered a dislocation. It looked eerily similar to that injury which caused him to be sidelined him five weeks last season.

Backup quarterback Marcus Mariota took over, and he will undoubtedly steer the ship home. While Daniels hasn't yet been officially ruled out, it's all but likely he'll miss the rest of this game, and some additional time. He was carted off, and FOX Sports sideline reporter Tom Rinaldi said he went for X-rays, and he is still there.

Daniels finished with 11 of 17 passing for 96 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions, while running seven times for 69 yards, including the final ill-fated run on his last play of the day.

Why it Matters: With Daniels sidelined, Mariota will take over. That changes things for the Washington offense, and it takes some fantasy appeal away from receivers like Terry McLaurin , Stefon Diggs , etc. There might be more of a run-based offense with Rachaad White and Jacory Croskey-Merritt .

articles.title: Waterdogs dominate Outlaws to win second PLL Championship
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Waterdogs talked all season about saving their best for the biggest moment. On Sunday, they finally did it. Philadelphia defeated the Denver...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Waterdogs talked all season about saving their best for the biggest moment.

Philadelphia defeated the Denver Outlaws 14-4 in the U.S. Bank PLL Championship at Sports Illustrated Stadium, winning the second championship in team history and completing its Bill Tierney-led turnaround.

Two years after finishing 2-8 in Tierney's first season as head coach, the Waterdogs saved their best performance for the biggest game of the season. They overwhelmed Denver from the opening whistle, built a 7-3 lead after one quarter and never let the Outlaws back into the game.

"We were building all year for something like this," Michael Sowers said. "We've got a great thing going, and I think today to be able to cap it off like this, it's just an unbelievable feeling. So it's hard to describe, but it's special."

Philadelphia had talked throughout the season about finding different ways to win. On Sunday, it did not need any of them.

The Waterdogs won on all three phases. They forced Denver into 13 turnovers by halftime, held the Outlaws to one shot on goal in the second quarter and shut them out in the third.

The result was a championship game that was effectively decided before the fourth quarter began.

For Championship MVP CJ Kirst , it was also the perfect ending to a season in which he became the league's MVP and broke the single-season goals record.

On his 24th birthday, Kirst scored seven points (5G, 2A), setting a PLL Championship record. He scored three times in the opening quarter and had four goals and an assist by halftime before continuing his historic performance after the break.

Yet Kirst said the performance was a reflection of the entire group.

"All credit goes to Coach [Dylan] Sheridan for coming up with a great game plan, but more so, just not changing anything up," Kirst said. "We have the guys; we've won in so many different ways. … Getting hot in the first quarter — that's really all it took. We just didn't have to think too much. Every huddle was one voice."

It was exactly the kind of collective performance the Waterdogs had spent the season building toward.

Gavin Adler , last season's Defensive Player of the Year, said the championship was the product of the intensity Philadelphia brought throughout the season.

"In these big games, X's and O's are valuable, but … the intensity you play with this group, it's way more significant than any X's and O's," Adler said. "I think you saw that really come out today. You saw the want from this group. I'm just so proud of the guys … we've been building, we've been through a lot too."

That history made Sunday's victory mean more than another championship.

The Waterdogs had been through injuries, lineup changes and the growing pains that came with building one of the league's youngest rosters. Dylan Hess suffered an ACL injury in Week 1. The team switched goalies in July. Rookies were asked to become starters immediately.

Instead of breaking the team apart, those moments became part of its identity.

Tierney pointed back to the team's 2-8 season in 2024 when asked when he realized this group could become something special.

"Well, I'll tell you the point we felt like we had something special is when two years ago we went two and eight," Tierney said. "And then all of a sudden started feeling good about ourselves, and then the Archers stepped in and humbled us again. But after that, you know, the way these guys adopted the young guys, the way Sean [Byrne] stepped up … I think for each guy to all of a sudden realize, 'Wow, we can do this.'"

Against Denver, Byrne continued his third-quarter dominance with six saves and no goals allowed. After becoming the starter mid-season, the undrafted rookie goalie went 7-0 and recorded a 68.4% save percentage.

For Tierney, who entered the professional game after winning seven national championships in college, the victory carried a different feeling because of the people who helped him get there.

"It's the people," Tierney said. "It's relying on people, relying on the conversations with Gavin every Monday, with Kieran [McArdle] every Monday, just to get them going. Obviously, these two guys [Sowers and Kirst] and Coach Sheridan just pulling this thing together. And there was never a guy — not once the whole season — who didn't believe in what we were doing."

Sowers, who starred for Philadelphia's 2022 championship team, had a front-row seat for the transformation.

"It's amazing," Sowers said. "I think having the opportunity to win, celebrate the guys, and then look over and see my brothers, my mom, my best friends who made the trip, and so many family friends, as well … it definitely means a lot to me, knowing that they're here to support me."

For Adler, who won a championship with the New York Atlas last year before joining Philadelphia, this one felt different because of the investment he made in the Waterdogs and the relationships he built along the way.

"With the longer season, everything, just the build of it, I've never really experienced that, and I've obviously had a little bit of a bigger hand in it this year, just being an older guy in the group," Adler said. "So it definitely means a lot more, and I'm just so excited for the future."

After everything Philadelphia had gone through to get there, Tierney said there was no better way to finish.

"To have them be able to save their best to last, we've been talking about that for a long time," Tierney said. "Save their best to last at both ends of the field with the faceoff game, the riding play. It's heck of a way to culminate a great season."

articles.title: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels injures the same left elbow he dislocated last year
articles.summary: Jayden Daniels was taken off on a cart and ruled out for the game after the Washington Commanders quarterback injured his left elbow on a botched play agains...
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Jayden Daniels was taken off on a cart and ruled out for the game after the Washington Commanders quarterback injured his left elbow on a botched play against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday.

Daniels missed all but one game in the second half of last season after dislocating his left elbow in a blowout loss to Seattle last November. That injury occurred when Daniels used his left arm while trying to brace himself on a fall, and the same thing happened on Sunday.

The Commanders were trying to score from the Dallas 1-yard line with 3 seconds remaining before halftime when left guard Chris Paul stepped on Daniels' foot as he backed away from center.

Daniels braced himself with his left arm and threw a wild pass that was incomplete as time expired. Daniels stayed down momentarily after the play, then started to walk to the sideline before going to the turf again.

Upon seeing a video replay of the injury, Fox NFL analyst Tom Brady uttered a profanity.

Daniels' head was covered in a towel as the cart left the field several minutes after all the Dallas players and most of the Washington players had gone to their locker rooms.

Daniels endured several injuries last season after he was honored as NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2024. The elbow injury came after earlier issues with a knee and hamstring.

articles.title: Tom Brady had just 2 words after seeing Jayden Daniels’ brutal injury live
articles.summary: Jayden Daniels’ injury looked so brutal that Tom Brady swore on national TV.
articles.body:
The last thing Washington Commanders fans wanted to see early on this season was yet another Jayden Daniels injury. Unfortunately, the Commanders quarterback ended Sunday's first half in the most brutal way possible that even Tom Brady couldn't help but swear on national television.

At the end of the second quarter, Daniels led the Commanders down the field looking to tie up the Dallas Cowboys , who held a 17-10 lead in their Week 2 matchup. While executing a third-and-goal play at the 1-yard line, Daniels tripped coming out of the snap and caught his fall with his left arm, causing his elbow to extend awkwardly. Daniels finished out the play with a desperation heave that fell incomplete, but ended up being carted off the field due to the injury to end the half. The Commanders then announced that Daniels' day was done.

In reviewing the Commanders' final play of the half and Daniels' injury in a slow-mo replay, Fox broadcaster Tom Brady couldn't help his strong verbal reaction to seeing Washington's quarterback go down in such a brutal fashion.

That about sums it up, yeah. This isn't Daniels' first go-around with an injury to this arm either, as he dislocated his left elbow in November 2025 after taking a hard sack. Daniels did return for one more game after the injury last season, but ended up being shut down for the season by the Commanders in mid-December.
